verses.text: I want you to know how hard I'm working for you, for the believers in Laodicea, and for everyone who hasn't met me face to face.
My goal is for them to be encouraged and united in love, and to enjoy the full confidence that comes from understanding, so they can know God's mystery—Christ himself.
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ.
I'm telling you this so no one can mislead you with clever arguments.
Though I'm away in body, I'm with you in spirit, and I'm glad to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
So then, just as you received Christ Jesus as Lord, keep living your lives in him.
Stay rooted and built up in him, firm in the faith you were taught, and overflowing with gratitude.
Watch out that no one captures you with empty, deceptive philosophy based on human traditions and the principles of this world rather than on Christ.
All the fullness of God lives in Christ in bodily form,
and you have been brought to fullness in him. He is the head over every ruler and authority.
In him you were also circumcised—not by human hands, but by putting off the sinful nature, through the circumcision done by Christ.
You were buried with Christ in baptism, and raised with him through faith in God's power, the God who raised him from the dead.
You were dead in your trespasses and in your uncircumcised human nature, but God made you alive with Christ and forgave all our trespasses.
He erased the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. He took it away by nailing it to the cross.
He disarmed rulers and authorities and exposed them publicly, triumphing over them through the cross.
So don't let anyone judge you about what you eat or drink, or about a festival, a new moon, or a Sabbath.
These are only shadows of what was coming; the reality is found in Christ.
Don't let anyone disqualify you by insisting on false humility and the worship of angels. Such people go on about visions they've supposedly seen and become arrogant for no reason.
They aren't holding on to Christ, the head. From him the whole body is nourished and held together by its joints and ligaments, and it grows as God makes it grow.
Since you died with Christ to the principles of this world, why do you submit to its rules as if you still belonged to it?
‘Don't handle! Don't taste! Don't touch!’
These rules are about things that disappear with use. They're based on human commands and teachings.
Such rules look wise because of their self-made worship, false humility, and harsh treatment of the body, but they don't restrain the desires of our human nature.
